questions.q: What did "steam-engine" drivers seem to think a horse was like?
choices: A steam-engine, only smaller
A pet dog that loves to run
A wild animal that must be tamed
A child that must be scolded
questions.evidence: a horse was something like a steam-engine, only smaller

questions.q: Why did steam-engine drivers refuse to get out and walk up steep hills?
choices: They had paid to ride, so they would ride
They were too old and tired to walk uphill
They were afraid of getting lost on foot
The horse would not stop to let them out
questions.evidence: they have paid to ride, and ride they will

questions.q: Why would Beauty rather go twenty miles with a good driver than ten with a steam-engine driver?
choices: The steam-engine style wore horses out faster
Good drivers always went at a slow walk
Steam-engine drivers paid the master less
The ten-mile drives were always uphill
questions.evidence: This steam-engine style of driving wears us up faster than any other kind

questions.q: What mistake did these drivers make with the brake?
choices: They forgot to take it off at the bottom of the hill
They put it on hard when going up the hill
They broke it on purpose so they could go faster
They pulled it on whenever they went up a steep hill
questions.evidence: they often forget to take it off at the bottom of the hill

choices: The horse paired with Beauty when two were needed
The man who drove the gig at the sharp corner
The owner of the livery stables in Bath
The young groom who looked after Beauty at the stables
questions.evidence: Rory was the horse that mostly went with me when a pair was ordered

questions.q: What happened to Rory at the sharp corner?
choices: A gig shaft ran into his chest
He slipped on the ice and fell
He was struck by a train at a crossing
He ran into the hedge in the dark
questions.evidence: The gig shaft ran right into the chest

questions.q: What was wrong with the driver who crashed into Rory?
choices: He did not know which side of the road to keep to
He had fallen asleep with the reins in his lap
He was nearly blind and could not see the corner
His horse had bolted and run away with him
questions.evidence: who don't even know which is their own side of the road

questions.q: What happened to Rory after his wound healed?
choices: He was sold for coal-carting
He went back to work beside Beauty
He was given to a vicar in the country
He was turned out to rest in a meadow

questions.q: Why did Peggy have such an odd, awkward pace?
choices: Her legs were short and she was whipped to keep up
She had a stone stuck in her shoe for weeks
She had never been properly trained to trot
She had hurt her leg when a gig shaft ran into her
questions.evidence: it is just because my legs are so short

questions.q: Peggy spoke "in a desponding tone." What does "desponding" mean here?
choices: Sad and without hope
Excited and full of joy
Angry and very loud
Proud and boastful
questions.evidence: said Peggy, in a desponding tone

questions.q: What was Peggy's first master, the young clergyman, like?
choices: Kind, and he never whipped her for not going faster
Always in a hurry and quick to use the whip
A farmer who drove home late from market
Rough and impatient, always shouting at her to hurry
questions.evidence: he never scolded or whipped me for not going faster

questions.q: How did Peggy's time with the farmer end?
choices: His gig turned over and he broke his arm
He sold her back to the young clergyman
She ran away from his farm one stormy night
He moved away and sold all his horses
questions.evidence: He was thrown out and his arm broken

questions.q: How did Peggy's life turn out after she was sold to two ladies?
choices: She was happy, going at a steady pace
She became lame and was put out to grass
She was sold again to pull coal carts
She grew bad-tempered and kicked
questions.evidence: looking as gay and contented as a horse could be

questions.q: According to the old gentleman, why should you never whip a horse for shying?
choices: It is afraid, and whipping only frightens it more
It teaches the horse to be lazy and slow
It breaks the whip and wastes the driver's money
It is against the law to whip horses in Bath
questions.evidence: he shies because he is frightened, and you only frighten him more

questions.q: What did the tall gentleman in Pulteney Street ask the hostler to take off?
choices: The curb
The saddle
The blinkers
The collar
questions.evidence: I don't like it," said the gentleman; "be so good as to take it off

questions.q: What is the main idea of this chapter?
choices: Careless driving harms horses; gentle driving helps them
Horses really enjoy pulling heavy loads up steep hills
Short-legged horses should never be used for driving
Horses should always be driven as fast as they can go uphill
questions.evidence: I found I had some one behind me who knew how a good horse ought to be driven
